sections.title: Habitat and form
sections.text: Yellow water-lily is an aquatic perennial of ponds, lakes and slow-moving water. Its creeping rhizome is about 3–8 cm across. The floating leaves are about 15–30 × 10–22 cm.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: The yellow flowers are about 4–5 cm across. The main conspicuous floral parts are sepals; numerous smaller petals lie inside them. The fruit is about 2.5 cm long and contains seeds about 5 mm long.

sections.title: Uses and cautions
sections.text: A traditional food use of the rhizome after cooking is reported, but the plant contains alkaloids and should not be eaten raw. Avoid concentrated preparations and do not treat this historical use as a general recommendation.
